title: Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
concept: Absolute value measures distance from zero, so it is never negative. Solving |expression| = k (with k > 0) means the inside can be either +k OR -k — that's TWO equations, and forgetting the second one is the number-one mistake here. So |x - 3| = 7 gives x - 3 = 7 (x = 10) and x - 3 = -7 (x = -4). Two special cases: |expression| = 0 has exactly one solution (the inside equals 0), and |expression| = (a negative number) has NO solution, because a distance can't be negative. For inequalities: |expression| ≤ k means the inside is trapped between -k and k (a single band, -k ≤ inside ≤ k), while |expression| ≥ k means the inside is at least k away in either direction (two separate rays). The SAT tests whether you produce both cases and read the boundary correctly.

steps: Split into two cases: x + 2 = 9 OR x + 2 = -9.
The solutions are x = 7 and x = -11. Check: |7 + 2| = 9 and |-11 + 2| = |-9| = 9.
|inside| ≤ k becomes a single band: -5 ≤ x - 1 ≤ 5.
Add 1 to all three parts: -4 ≤ x ≤ 6.
So x is between -4 and 6, inclusive.

trapPatterns: Solving only the positive case and forgetting the negative case — the single most common absolute-value error.
Treating |expression| = (negative) as if it has solutions; a distance is never negative, so there are none.
Sign errors inside the bars: mishandling the shift (e.g. solving x + 3 = -5 as x = -2 instead of -8).
Reporting the wrong end of the solution set — giving the least solution when asked for the greatest, or vice versa.
For inequalities, confusing the '≤ k' single-band case with the '≥ k' two-ray case, or dropping the shift inside the bars.
calculatorStrategy: Desmos handles both cases at once: type the equation as y1 = |expression| and y2 = k, and both intersection x-values are the two solutions; for an inequality, type it directly (e.g. abs(x-1)<=5) and read the shaded band. By hand, the discipline is always: write BOTH cases before solving either. The negative case is where points are won and lost.

problems.question: What is the greatest value of x that satisfies |x - 4| = 6?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: Reported the least solution (x = 4 - 6) instead of the greatest.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: Ignored the shift and read x = 6 straight off the right-hand side.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: Subtracted 4 from 6 instead of adding it to 4.

explanation: Split into two cases: x - 4 = 6 or x - 4 = -6.
The greatest of the two solutions is 10.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Desmos: y=abs(x-4) and y=6 intersect at x=-2 and x=10; the greater is 10.

problems.question: What is the least value of x that satisfies |x + 3| = 5?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: Gave the greatest solution (x = -3 + 5), not the least.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: Solved the negative case x + 3 = -5 as x = -2 (added 3 instead of subtracting).

choices.label: D
choices.trap: Sign error: wrote x = 3 + 5 = 8 for the negative case.

explanation: Split into two cases: x + 3 = 5 or x + 3 = -5.
The least of the two solutions is -8.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Desmos: y=abs(x+3) and y=5 meet at x=-8 and x=2; the lesser is -8.

problems.question: What is the greatest value of x that satisfies |2x| = 14?
problems.calculatorStrategy: Divide out: |2x| = 14 means |x| = 7, so x = ±7; the greatest is 7.

problems.question: What is the sum of all solutions to |x - 5| = 9?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: Reported only the positive-case solution, x = 14.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: Treated the solutions as ±9, ignoring the shift by 5, so they cancel.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: Reported only the negative-case solution, x = -4.

explanation: Two cases: x - 5 = 9 → x = 14, and x - 5 = -9 → x = -4.
Shortcut: the two solutions are symmetric about the shift 5, so their sum is 2 · 5 = 10.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Find both intersections in Desmos (x=14, x=-4) and add. The solutions always average to the shift value.

problems.question: What is the greatest value of x that satisfies |x - 2| ≤ 6?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: Reported the least value of the band instead of the greatest.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: Dropped the -2 and solved |x| ≤ 6 as x ≤ 6.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: Subtracted 2 from 6 instead of adding it to 2.

explanation: The greatest value in the band is 8.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Desmos: abs(x-2)<=6 shades the band from -4 to 8; read the right edge, 8.

problems.question: What is the greatest value of x that satisfies |3x - 6| = 12?
problems.calculatorStrategy: Solve both cases by hand, or read the right intersection of y=abs(3x-6) and y=12 in Desmos (x=6).

problems.question: What is the product of all solutions to |x + 1| = 4?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: Sign error; multiplied the two solutions as if they had the same sign.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: Reported only one solution (the negative case) instead of the product.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: Computed (-1) - 16 instead of (-1)² - 16 when using the shortcut.

explanation: Two cases: x + 1 = 4 → x = 3, and x + 1 = -4 → x = -5.
Shortcut: for |x - h| = k the roots are h ± k, so the product is h² - k² = (-1)² - 4² = 1 - 16 = -15.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Read both intersections (x=3, x=-5) in Desmos and multiply. The product equals h² - k² where h is the shift and k the right side.

problems.question: What is the least integer value of x that satisfies |2x + 1| < 9?
explanation: The inequality is strict, so x = -5 is excluded; the least integer is -4.
problems.calculatorStrategy: Desmos: abs(2x+1)<9 shades -5 < x < 4 with open ends; the least integer strictly inside is -4.
